title: Language button's accessible name doesn't contain its visible text (WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name)
stepsToReproduce:
1. Open any page (logged in or not).
2. Run axe (TC-NF-03, Playwright + @axe-core/playwright).
3. Inspect the language button in the app bar.
expected: The button's accessible name starts with the text it shows (EN or VI), so voice-control users can say "click EN".
actual: The button shows EN but is named "Đổi ngôn ngữ sang English". axe reports label-content-name-mismatch (serious) on every page.
rootCause: LanguageSwitch.tsx set aria-label to the translated hint only, which replaced the visible text as the accessible name.
fix: The aria-label now starts with the visible text: `${next.toUpperCase()} – ${t('language.switch')}`. Tests that looked the button up by its old exact name now use a regex (App.test.tsx, CategoriesPage.test.tsx).
filesOrCommit: client/src/components/LanguageSwitch.tsx; fix d4d8e75 in PR #33, merged as b14493c
evidence: https://github.com/dangnguyenducanh/Zalo-Tele-intergrated-financial-apps/pull/33 ; retest: RUN-006 on b14493c, TC-NF-03 passed in light and dark, full suite green

title: E2E bot tests call the real Telegram Bot API from the test server
stepsToReproduce:
1. npm run test:e2e (no bot token in the environment).
2. Watch the E2E API server log while client/e2e/bot.spec.ts runs.
expected: The E2E server never leaves the machine: outbound Telegram/Zalo Bot API calls are stubbed and recorded, so tests are hermetic and can't message real chats.
actual: server/src/bot/telegram.js:8 posts to https://api.telegram.org/bot<empty>/sendMessage; Telegram answers 404, the error is caught and logged, and the specs still pass. With a real token in the environment they would message real chat IDs.
rootCause: server/test/helpers/e2e-server.js only swaps MongoDB for an in-memory one; it doesn't stub outbound HTTP the way the Vitest suites do with MSW.
fix: The E2E server now loads a stub before the app starts (server/test/helpers/bot-api-stub.js): Telegram and Zalo Bot API calls get a fake successful answer shaped like the real API and are recorded (method + chat id, never the token); any other non-local host throws. Production code is unchanged.
filesOrCommit: server/test/helpers/bot-api-stub.js, server/test/helpers/e2e-server.js, server/test/e2e-server.test.js; fix 1e8e8e1 in PR #35, merged as da6ad6a
evidence: Test-run report RUN-006 (E2E server log line: telegram webhook update failed: Error: Telegram sendMessage failed: 404 Not Found) ; fix: https://github.com/dangnguyenducanh/Zalo-Tele-intergrated-financial-apps/pull/35 ; retest: RUN-008 on da6ad6a, TC-NF-11 passed (3/3), no request to api.telegram.org or bot-api.zaloplatforms.com in the E2E run

title: A refresh cut off after the server rotated the token logs the user out on every device
stepsToReproduce:
1. Log in on staging.
2. Open /bot and, as soon as its start-up POST /api/auth/refresh is sent, navigate to /transactions (or reload, or lose the network).
3. The next page load sends the old refresh cookie.
expected: A refresh whose answer was lost (navigation, reload, flaky network) does not end the session; only a real token reuse (a stolen copy) revokes every session.
actual: The server already rotated the token, so the old cookie is treated as theft: 401, and every session of the user is revoked, including a second device that did nothing. Seen 3 times during the charter run on an unstable network.
rootCause: server/src/services/auth.js refresh(): any reuse of a rotated token revokes all sessions (docs/04 §4.3 'Reuse detection'), with no grace window for a lost response.
fix: Approved by the student on 2026-11-21 ("Yes, 30 s grace"). refresh() in server/src/services/auth.js now gives reuse a 30 s grace window: a rotated token that comes back within 30 s while its replacement has never been refreshed is a lost answer, so the unused replacement is revoked and the token is rotated once more (both old rows point at the new session). Any other reuse still revokes every session. docs/04 §4.3 updated.
evidence: charter-runs/2026-11-21/BUG-refresh-abort.mp4, BUG-refresh-abort.log, repro-refresh-abort.mjs, MT-03.attempt1.mp4 (local, git-ignored) ; retest on staging with the fix deployed, same repro script: charter-runs/2026-11-21/retest-T21/ (BUG-003-retest.mp4, .log): the next refresh answers 200, the user stays on /transactions, the untouched second device refreshes 200

title: Bot inbox still lists a draft that was confirmed in the chat, until a reload
stepsToReproduce:
1. Open Hộp thư bot with a Zalo draft waiting.
2. Leave the page, type "ok" in Zalo (the bot confirms it).
3. Open Hộp thư bot again from the menu.
actual: The old list is shown; pressing Xác nhận gives 409 ALREADY_CONFIRMED ("Giao dịch này đã được xác nhận."); a reload fixes it.
rootCause: RTK Query served the cached GET /transactions?status=draft result for 60 s. Drafts also change in the chats, which no web mutation's tags cover.
fix: DraftList asks the server again each time the inbox opens (refetchOnMountOrArgChange).
evidence: found: MT-03_stale-draft-after-ok.png, MT-03.mp4; retest on staging with the fix deployed: charter-runs/2026-11-21/retest-T20/ (BUG-004_*.png, retest-T20.mp4): 0 drafts after coming back, no 409

title: After switching to English, the dashboard keeps Vietnamese category names until a reload
stepsToReproduce:
1. Dashboard in Vietnamese with spending this month.
2. Click EN in the app bar.
3. Look at "Spending by category".
expected: Category names in English (Food & drinks, Transport).
actual: "Ăn uống" and "Đi lại" stay until a full reload.
rootCause: GET /stats/by-category names each category in the profile's language (server/src/services/stats.js), but PATCH /users/me invalidated no RTK Query tags, so the statistics loaded in Vietnamese stayed cached. (Other endpoints send both names and the browser picks one.)
fix: updateMe invalidates the Stats tag when a new language is saved, so the statistics on screen are fetched again.
evidence: found: MT-05_phone-dark-en-dashboard-full.png vs …-after-reload.png; retest on staging with the fix deployed: charter-runs/2026-11-21/retest-T20/ (BUG-005_*.png, retest-T20.mp4): English names right after the switch

title: A refresh running in parallel with "revoke every session" keeps its new session alive
stepsToReproduce:
1. Log in, refresh A → B.
2. Within 30 s send two refreshes with A at the same moment (or a reuse of A in parallel with a refresh of B).
3. Count the user's active sessions.
expected: One request is treated as theft, so every session of the user is revoked and none stays active.
actual: The winner's new session stays active after the "revoke all" (about 3 runs in 5 in the reviewer's repro).
rootCause: revokeAllSessions is one updateMany on revokedAt: null. A parallel refresh that had already claimed its old session called openSession() after that updateMany had passed, so its new row was never matched (server/src/services/sessions.js, auth.js rotate()).
fix: revokeAllSessions first stamps users.sessionsRevokedAt, then revokes. Every session carries chainStartedAt (the time of the login that began its rotation chain, copied forward on each rotation). rotate() re-reads the stamp and status after openSession(); if the stamp is not older than the chain's login, it revokes the new session and answers 401 INVALID_REFRESH (403 ACCOUNT_LOCKED after an admin lock). Comparing with the chain's login rather than the newest session also closes the gap the PR #50 review found: a session created while the stamp was being written is younger than the stamp, but its chain is not.
evidence: TC-F1-20 (4 cases): pausing Session.create makes the interleaving deterministic; the 2 interleaving cases failed before the fix (200, one session alive), and the 'session younger than the stamp' case failed against the first version of the fix (200). All pass now; 40 real parallel retries left 0 active sessions.
